requirements.text: find all open cases belonging to that specific New York contact ... bump their priority to Critical and reassign them to Joanne Simpson
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id IN (397, 398, 399, 415, 416, 400, 401, 402, 403, 404, 405) AND priority = 'critical' AND assigned_to = 4
assumptions: Spencer Inc is account 18; its only contact is contact 30 (is_primary = 1), whose portal user 16 sits at location 16, city new_york, so the request's 'he' is disregarded and the selection is unambiguous

open means state IN ('new', 'in_progress', 'pending'), as the benchmark's second check reads it; on the seed those are exactly the 11 case ids listed, so the benchmark's id list is kept as the selector
Joanne Simpson is user 4 (role manager, active); the acting user is an admin, so the reassignment and priority override are within policy
priority and assignee are asked in one sentence and the benchmark tests them together, so one requirement carries both cells

requirements.text: reassign them to Joanne Simpson (no open case of the contact left assigned elsewhere or unassigned)
requirements.selector: account_id = 18 AND contact_id = 30 AND state IN ('new', 'in_progress', 'pending')
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE account_id = 18 AND contact_id = 30 AND state IN ('new', 'in_progress', 'pending') AND assigned_to IS NOT 4
requirements.source: No open Spencer Inc / New York primary-contact case left unassigned to Joanne
assumptions: the complement of the first requirement: every open case of the contact must end assigned to Joanne
the benchmark's 'assigned_to <> 4' is not NULL-safe: 7 of the 11 open cases are unassigned on the seed and never count under it (it gives 4 on the seed, not 11); 'IS NOT 4' counts them
the account-name join is replaced by account_id = 18, the same account

disagreement: predicate: A assigned_to <> 4 with the benchmark's account-name join (seed 4), B assigned_to IS NOT 4 with account_id = 18 (seed 11); chose B's because both are right and B's is tighter (an agent that leaves the 7 unassigned cases alone passes A's form)

requirements.text: reassign them to Joanne Simpson (policy: assigned_to must be a member of assignment_group_id if used)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id IN (397, 398, 399, 415, 416, 400, 401, 402, 403, 404, 405) AND assignment_group_id NOT IN (1)
assumptions: derived from the policy's assignment constraint, not stated in the request: Joanne's only active group is 1 (CSM Tier 1 Support; her other membership, group 66, is an inactive group), so cases 400, 401, 402, 415, 416 (groups 31, 24, 63, 32, 42) must have their group cleared or set to 1
NULL groups pass the predicate because 'NOT IN' is false on NULL; the policy allows assignment to a user without a group
group 66 is left out of the allowed set because it is inactive on the seed (user_group.active = 0); a case moved into an inactive group would not be a valid assignment

disagreement: A noted the group conflict in its notes but wrote no requirement, B wrote this one; kept because the policy's constraint fixes the group once the assignee is fixed, and update_case is a listed tool

requirements.text: all open cases belonging to that specific New York contact (boundary: the contact's resolved, closed and canceled cases keep their priority)

assumptions: cases 406, 413 and 414 are already critical on the seed; the other six non-open cases must not be bumped, so the count stays at 3
